disclosures.name: TestMulUnbalanced
disclosures.reason: A MemStats BYTES meter, not an AllocsPerRun one: allocBytes reads runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc around one nat.mul of a 50,000-word by a 40-word operand and asserts the bytes stay under 10 times the inputs' size. It read pass|pass at go1.24.13; go1.26.10 hands nat.mul a preallocated getStack() stack, which is how Go stays near 1x (its one ~400 KB result). ROOTED by G at f8fe15c97e, with a thread-precise probe inside the converted test (scratch, never committed). The stack is reused correctly: save, nat and restore cost 0 bytes. The excess is about 4.2 KB in each of the ~1,249 40x40 products. 74% of it is one converted construct: an element address-of whose only use is an identity compare. alias()'s `&x[cap-1] == &y[cap-1]` mints two 184-byte element boxes per call and nat.mul calls it twice, across four mul frames per product (2,944 B); addVW's `&z[0] != &x[0]` adds 144 B. Another 21% is karatsuba's nine non-escaping `&Int{...}` locals at 96 B each (864 B, the REC-B class). The rest is karatsuba's defer (~216 B) and basicMul (56 B). Go allocates none of these.
disclosures.want: allocated bytes / input bytes <= 10 (runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc around one nat.mul)
disclosures.reading: 5,723,096 B for a 400,320 B input, a ratio of 14 (windows/amd64, f8fe15c97e, Release untiered, the row filtered to ^TestMulUnbalanced$). A thread-precise reading of the same call is 5,722,800 B = 400,376 (the result) + about 1,249 x 4.2 KB. Unit: BYTES (lesson 63: the alloc-units extractor records AllocsPerRun units only)
disclosures.plan: INCREMENT 1 (queued post-publish, COORD 2026-10-25): an allocation-free identity compare for `&a[i] ==/!= &b[j]`, where golib compares the backing storage and absolute index with ж=='s semantics and the converter emits it when both operands are element address-ofs. It is predicted to bring 4.2 KB per product to ~1.2 KB and the ratio to ~5 < 10, retiring this entry alone. Then docs/phase4/DESIGN-nonescaping-locals.md (REC-B) for the Int locals.

disclosures.name: TestNewIntAllocs
disclosures.reason: A want-zero AllocsPerRun assert over `x.Add(x, NewInt(n))`: NewInt is arranged to inline so that its `&Int{...}` and its one-word abs slice live on Go's stack. The divergence is an ORACLE-side change, not a C# regression. The test body, NewInt and Int.Add are byte-for-byte the same at go1.24.13 and go1.26.10, and the go1.24.13 page reads `fail | fail`: Go failed this test too, so it matched. At go1.26.10 Go passes it, and C# still allocates, so it now reads Go=pass / C#=fail.
disclosures.reading: got 1 allocation per run (windows/amd64, f8fe15c97e, H-3's pass-1 reading as forwarded by COORD). The per-n lines are owed to the alloc-units extractor run.
disclosures.plan: docs/phase4/DESIGN-nonescaping-locals.md (REC-B): the candidate site is the ж<Int> box of the inlined NewInt result, which Go keeps on the stack. The extractor run's per-n lines confirm whether the abs slice adds a second site for n != 0.
